newsitem.title: UK: Euro HS fuel oil quiet and stable as LS weakens.
newsitem.headline: Euro HS fuel oil quiet and stable as LS weakens.

text.p: European fuel markets were deadly quiet on Wednesday with high sulphur values stable and low sulphur prices under pressure, traders said.

High sulphur barges stayed in the $90/$92 a tonne range, trading twice at $90.50 in Antwerp. But poor bunker demand did little to keep dealers at their desks as the market sleep walked into the depths of summer.

"It was extremely boring, there was less than 10kt of bunker demand," said one trader. Overall market strength persists, however, on a scarcity of supply, with less Russian fuel having arrived in Rotterdam up till now than was anticipated.

But that may change and bring price pressure onto the scene, with 6 or 7 cargoes of cracked Russian material due to load in the Baltic ports by the end of next week and expected to be offered into the ARA area.
"There will be a flurry and we'll see what happens when they show up," said one trader. Cracked Russian M100 cargoes were talked on offer at a dollar above the two means quote.
A British major was offering a small cargo of one percent fuel at $92-$93 fob, but other traders insisted the price slide on low sulphur had not yet gone so far.
Some were offering late August cargoes at $95-$96, which in turn was described as unrealistic, and fair value was pegged at $93-$94 a tonne.
